Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:46: "A lowly spirit" is the attribute called "spirit," and it is well known - and it says "lowly" since we find (Psalms 34:19), "the LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and He saves the contrite of spirit," and likewise (Isaiah 57:15), "high and holy I dwell, and with the contrite and lowly of spirit."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:47: "A humble soul" - in the place of Nefesh, which is the place of lowliness, and the lowly poor who do not pursue desire - and here is the place of the poor and lowly, to whom the gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and corners were given, since all their portions are small: two omers is a forgotten sheaf, but three are not a forgotten sheaf; two stalks are gleanings, but three are not gleanings, and so on, as explained in the Mishnah (Pe'ah, chapter 6, mishnah 5). And so Ruth, who corresponds to this attribute, said (Ruth 2:2), "let me go, please, and glean among the ears of grain" - content with little, and not pursuing desire - and so Boaz said to her (ibid. 3:10), "you have made your last kindness better," and so on, "in not going after the young men, whether poor or rich" - behold, this too is the breaking of desire.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:48: Behold, these three include all the supernal attributes, and one can say that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, intended this in the teaching we copied at the beginning of the chapter: from the Torah, from the Prophets, and from the Writings we find, in every place where the might of the Holy One, blessed be He, is stated, His humility is recognized there. And the reason this matter comes in Torah, Prophets, and Writings can be said to correspond to the three places mentioned [Chochmah/Binah, and so on] - and there is a hint in the verses the author of the teaching brought, as the reader shall be precise about them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:49: And Rabbi Yosef Yavetz wrote that these three mentioned - "a good eye," and so on - correspond to Neshamah, Ru'ach, and Nefesh: "a good eye" corresponds to Neshamah, and therefore he lost the desire of this world, since he built his levels in heaven. "A lowly spirit" corresponds to Ru'ach, this is humility. "A humble soul" corresponds to Nefesh. And he wrote that whoever is complete in these attributes has three gates of the Garden of Eden opened for him, for his flesh shall rest securely in the grave and his soul shall be guarded, as it is said (Proverbs 6:22), "when you walk it shall guide you" - and as explained in the Zohar, his spirit [ru'ach] shall go to the lower Garden of Eden and his soul [neshamah] to Eden, and the head of the Garden of Eden is Abraham our father, peace be upon him - meaning, the father of holy souls, as the verse says (Malachi 2:10), "have we not all one father?" And whoever has the three attributes of the wicked Balaam has three gates of Gehinnom opened for him, for these three were emanated for Israel from the sefirah of purity, and for the nations of the world, idol worshippers, the opposite - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:50: And after we have explained, in this chapter, the general attributes of humility, which include all the attributes, as explained, we shall come in the next chapter to explain the punishments of pride and its blemish, so that a person distance himself from pride, whether out of love or fear of anger - and since it is better that a person do his deeds for the sake of Heaven, out of love, to resemble his Creator, we therefore preceded with the previous chapter:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:1: Just as humility is one of the great virtues of the soul, such that to merit it several attributes must precede it, as we explained in the Gate of Love (chapter 11), concerning the teaching of Rabbi Pinchas (Avodah Zarah 20b), "purity leads to holiness," and according to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, humility is greater than all of them - so pride is an attribute that lowers the soul from the place of supernal holiness down to the lowest level, as it is written (Proverbs 29:23), "a man's pride shall bring him low" - and so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Tractate Avodah Zarah, first chapter (18b): Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, whoever is arrogant falls into Gehinnom, as it is said (Proverbs 21:24), "proud, haughty, scoffer is his name, who acts with wanton arrogance" - and there is no "arrogance" [evrah] except Gehinnom, as it is said (Zephaniah 1:15), "a day of wrath [evrah] is that day" - to this point. And it used the language of "falling," to show that it is like the way of those who fall, who fall from a high place to a low place, and there is nothing lower than Gehinnom - and the sign of this matter is, there is nothing higher than ONEG [delight] and nothing lower than NEGA [affliction/plague] (see Sefer Yetzirah, chapter 2, mishnah 7).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:2: And it is already known that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Tanchuma, Metzora 4) that afflictions [tzara'at] come for eleven things, one of them being haughtiness of spirit. And in Tanchuma (there) they proved this from Na'aman, and in one place (Vayikra Rabbah 17:3), from what is written (II Chronicles 26:16), "and when he was strong, his heart was lifted up, to his destruction," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:3: And the reason for this is that a person, from the beginning of his creation, was created only so that he recognize the greatness of the Holy One, blessed be He, and serve Him as a servant serving his master - for it is not fitting for a servant to be proud before his master; and behold, pride is fitting only before the Master of All, to whom all are subjugated, as explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 2. Now, all that is emanated, formed, and made acknowledges His providence and is subjugated to His word, knowing that all their vitality and flow is from Him, blessed be He. But whoever is proud indicates that he has no master - it follows that he uproots himself from the holy place to the place of impurity, [the place of] those who deny [divine] providence - for the serpent denied providence when he enticed Adam and his wife, saying (Genesis 3:5), "and you shall be like gods, knowing good and evil" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bereishit Rabbah 19:4) that the serpent said to her, from this tree the Holy One, blessed be He, ate and created the world, and He is jealous, and so on - behold, he taught duality [a second power], and denied the very essence of everything.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:4: And therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, commanded us (Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 4), "be exceedingly, exceedingly lowly of spirit" - for although in the other good attributes the moderate attribute is the best of attributes, in the matter of humility one must go to the very extreme, in a manner that he distance himself entirely from pride, so that no trace of the husk attach to him. And for this they said in Tractate Sotah (5a): Rav Nachman said, not of its own kind at all, not even in part - is it a small matter what is written of it (Proverbs 16:5), "every proud heart is an abomination to the LORD"? - to this point. And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained that he called it an abomination. And the explanation is, it is already known that "abomination" refers to idolatry, as it is written (Deuteronomy 7:26), "and you shall not bring an abomination into your house." And so it says shortly before this (4b), concerning the punishments of pride and haughtiness of spirit: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, whoever has haughtiness of spirit is as though he worships idols - it is written here, "every proud heart is an abomination to the LORD," and it is written there, "and you shall not bring an abomination into your house"; and Rabbi Yochanan himself said, it is as though he denies the foundational principle, as it is said (Deuteronomy 8:14), "and your heart becomes proud, and you forget the LORD your God," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:5: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said, it is as though he had committed all forbidden relations - it is written here, "every proud heart is an abomination to the LORD," and it is written there (Leviticus 18:27), "for the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations." Ulla said, it is as though he built a high place [for idol worship], as it is said (Isaiah 2:22), "cease from man, in whose nostrils is breath, for what [bameh] is he accounted?" - do not read "bameh" [what] but "bamah" [high place].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:6: Whence do we know the warning against the haughty of spirit? Rava said in the name Ze'iri: (Jeremiah 13:15), "hear and give ear, be not proud." Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak [derived it] from here (Deuteronomy 8:14), "and your heart becomes proud, and you forget the LORD your God," and it is written, "take heed to yourself, lest you forget the LORD your God" (ibid. 6:12) - and along the lines of Rabbi Avin's statement in the name of Rabbi Ela, for Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ela, wherever it says "take heed," "lest," or "do not," it is only [expressing] a negative commandment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:7: Rav Avira expounded - sometimes he said it in the name of Rabbi Asi, sometimes in the name of Rabbi Ami - every person who has haughtiness of spirit is eventually diminished, as it is said (Job 24:24), "they are exalted for a little while, then they are gone" - and lest you say, he still exists in the world - therefore Scripture says, "and are gone." And if he repents, he is gathered from the world in his own time, like Abraham our father, as it is said, "and they are brought low, they are gathered up like all others," like Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, of whom it is written, "in everything," "from everything," "everything." And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "diminished" - in his own importance. "They are exalted for a little while" - once their eminence is diminished. "He still exists in the world" - is sustained. "And they are brought low" - and if he returns and becomes lowly, humble, lowering himself. "Like all others" - like those of whom "all/everything" is said. "They are gathered up" - from the world, they die the death of the upright - of Abraham it is written (Genesis 24:1), "the LORD had blessed Abraham in everything [bakol]"; of Isaac it is written (ibid. 27:33), "and I ate from everything [mikol]"; of Jacob it is written (ibid. 33:11), "for God has favored me, and because I have everything [kol]" - and this is explicitly explained in Bereishit Rabbah - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:8: Further, there, the completion of the teaching mentioned - and if not [if he does not repent] (Job 24:24), "they are cut off like the top of an ear of grain" - what is "like the top of an ear of grain"? Rav Huna and Rav Chisda - one said, like the "beard" of the ear of grain [the topmost, brittle part]; the other said, like the ear of grain itself. Now, for the one who says "like the beard of the ear of grain," this fits with what is written, "like the top of an ear of grain" - but for the one who says "like the ear of grain itself," why "like the top of an ear of grain"? Rav Asi said, and so it was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael: a parable of a person entering his field - the tallest [stalks] he gathers first - to this point. And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: the "beard" of the ear of grain is the highest part, called "the beard of the ear," which breaks and falls off by itself. "The tallest he gathers" - and this is "they are cut off like the top of an ear of grain," like the ear whose head appears above its fellows.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:9: Further, there, Rabbi Elazar said, every person who has haughtiness of spirit deserves to be cut down like an Asherah [idolatrous tree] - it is written here (Isaiah 10:33), "and the lofty of stature shall be cut down," and it is written there (Deuteronomy 7:5), "and you shall cut down their Asherim." And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "like an Asherah" - it shall be cut down and its roots pursued, like an Asherah, which requires cutting down [and destroying] its root, as it is written (Deuteronomy 12:3), "and you shall destroy their name."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:10: Further, there, Rabbi Elazar said, every person who has haughtiness of spirit - his dust shall not be aroused [in the resurrection], as it is said (Isaiah 26:19), "awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust" - it does not say "you who lie in the dust," but "you who dwell in the dust" - one who made himself a neighbor to the dust in his lifetime. And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "aroused" - awakens at the resurrection of the dead. "You who lie in the dust" is not said, which would apply to all the dead; "a neighbor to the dust" - lowers himself even to the dust.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:11: And Rabbi Elazar said, every person who has haughtiness of spirit, the Shechinah wails over him, as it is said (Psalms 138:6), "and the haughty He knows from afar." And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "wails" - laments. "And the haughty He knows from afar" - the beginning of the verse is "for the LORD is exalted, yet He regards the lowly, and the haughty," and so on - "the haughty," "from afar," meaning many days before the punishment comes upon him, "He knows" - the Shechinah mourns and grieves over him, like (Judges 8:16), "and he made known to them [vayoda bahem] the men of Sukkoth" - "and he made known his widowhood" (Ezekiel 19:7) - "yoda" [known] as in bringing above (Psalms 74:5), a term of breaking.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:12: Rav Avira expounded, and some say Rabbi Elazar: come and see, the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not like the attribute of flesh and blood. The attribute of flesh and blood is that a high one sees a high one, but a high one does not see a lowly one - but the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so: He is high, and yet sees the lowly, as it is said, "for the LORD is exalted, yet He regards the lowly." And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "regards the lowly" - to draw him near and to strive with him, and he is considered important in His eyes, like (Hosea 9:10), "like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel, like the first fruit on the fig tree in its first season I saw your fathers" - I set My eyes upon them to draw them near and cherish them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:13: Rav Chisda said, and some say Mar Ukva: every person who has haughtiness of spirit, the Holy One, blessed be He, says, I and he cannot dwell together in the world, as it is said (Psalms 101:5), "whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will destroy; whoever has a haughty look and a proud heart, him [oto] I cannot [endure]" - do not read "oto" [him] but "ito" [with him] I cannot [dwell]. Some teach this concerning slanderers, as it is said, "whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will destroy" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:14: Further, there, Chizkiyah said, a person's prayer is heard only if he makes his heart like flesh, as it is said (Isaiah 66:23), "and it shall come to pass that from new moon to new moon, all flesh shall come." Rabbi Zeira said, "flesh" [tzara'at law] has "and he shall be healed" written of it, but "adam" [tzara'at law] does not have "and he shall be healed" written of it. And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "like flesh," which is soft, and not like stone, which is hard. "To bow down" - to pray - those who are like flesh shall come and pray, for they are heard before Me, but the haughty of spirit shall not come. "'Flesh' has 'and he shall be healed' written of it" - "or if flesh has in its skin a boil, and it is healed" (Leviticus 13:18); "if a man has in the skin of his flesh" (ibid. 13:2), "if the plague of leprosy be in a man" (ibid. 13:8) - "and he shall be healed" is not written in either of these; from your own reasoning you learn that whoever is soft and humble, like flesh, is close to being healed from sufferings that come upon him, but whoever is hard like the ground has no healing for his wounds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:15: Rabbi Yochanan said, ADAM [man]: ashes [efer], blood [dam], bile [marah]; BASAR [flesh]: shame [bushah], stench [sirachon], worm [rimah]. Some say: shame [bushah], the grave [she'ol], worm [rimah], for it is written with a Shin - to this point. And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: ADAM - why is he called ADAM? Because he is ashes, blood, bile - meaning, all of him is vapor, therefore he should not be proud. "Bile" is the bitter moisture that comes from the bitterness in the liver and increases in a person, all according to the months and the changing of times and according to the food he eats, and through it come illnesses, plagues, and pains - some, in the language of physicians, call it black bile, and some call it red bile. "She'ol" - the place he requests [she'ol] as his house, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:16: Further, there, Rav Ashi said, every person who has haughtiness of spirit is eventually brought low, as it is said (Leviticus 14:56), "and for a rising [se'et], and for a scab [sapachat], and for a bright spot" - and "se'et" means nothing but a rise, as it is said (Isaiah 2:13), "and upon all the high mountains, and upon all the raised hills"; and "sapachat" means nothing but something attached/lowly, as it is said (I Samuel 2:36), "attach me [saphcheni], please," and so on - to this point. Up to here the punishments mentioned there have been reached.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:17: And when a person takes to heart all the punishments mentioned - the greatest of the great being that he has no rising at the resurrection of the dead - he should lower the height of his pride, and take to heart that it would have been better for him not to have been created, since a person's proper remedy is that he live at the resurrection of the dead, as explained in the Gate of Love (chapter 6), and whoever is proud has attached himself so much to the husk that almost that body will not live [again].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:18: And besides all the punishments stated, when a person takes to heart what is mentioned at the end of the teachings mentioned, in Rabbi Yochanan's saying, that man is "flesh" - shame, stench, worm, or "flesh" - shame, the grave, worm - the intent is that there is no shame like the shame of sins when they are shown to him before the whole heavenly retinue, and upon seeing his evil deeds, shall he not then be ashamed and humiliated, with no mouth to answer and no forehead to lift his head, as the prophet said (Jeremiah 3:25), "let us lie down in our shame, and let our humiliation cover us, for we have sinned against the LORD our God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:19: "Stench" is because he is drawn after the desires of the world, and through this he stinks - and therefore it is fitting to distance oneself from the acquisitions of the world and the pursuit of excess, whose end is stench, and it is the excesses that bring about pride of heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:20: Or, when he considers that the place of She'ol is his house, then what has he to do with the world, and why should he be proud, when he is placed in the lowest of places - and if his sins should cause him to descend to Gehinnom, all the more so is it fitting for him to mourn and submit for his sins and lower the height of his pride, since this is his end if he does not repent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:21: "Worm" is a judgment among the judgments of the grave, as explained in the Gate of Fear - and when a person wishes to be proud of his beauty, his clothing, or his wealth, let him consider that the end of everything is that the worm shall eat it, and he shall not be proud of any worldly matter, since all its goodness has an end and ceases, being entirely clothed in the filth of the serpent that brought death to the world - and a person has nothing from this world except the mitzvot and the Torah, which are spiritual, and cleave to the spiritual, enduring soul, cleaving to its Creator, after its judgment is completed and it is made acceptable upon the altar through Michael the great prince, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Metzora, page 53b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:22: And so, among the things that bring about humility and lowliness is considering the greatness of our Creator, Creator of all, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose greatness is unfathomable and has no limit, as we elaborated in the Gate of Fear - and this shall bring about humility, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 8:4-5), "when I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers," and so on, "what is man that You remember him?" - for even the whole world under the dome of the firmament is like a mustard seed - if so, the people of the world within it are considered as nothing, as it is said (Daniel 4:32), "and all the inhabitants of the earth are considered as nothing."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:23: And if he is proud of his wisdom, let him think of the wisdom of the ancient sages, and then he shall see that all our wisdom is like the peel of garlic compared to their wisdom. And further, corresponding to wisdom there must be fear and deed, for "an error in learning is accounted as deliberate" (Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 13), as we elaborated on this in the Gate of Fear (chapter 4), as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Bereishit Rabbah (19:1) concerning "now the serpent was crafty" (Genesis 3:1) - they said, according to his wisdom was his downfall: "crafty" more than all, "cursed" more than all - and similarly to this (Ecclesiastes 1:18), "and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow" - for a stain falling on a silk garment is not comparable to a stain falling on a linen garment, for according to the preciousness of its value shall it be difficult to purify.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:24: And if he is proud of his wealth, he must fear lest the wealth be for his own harm, or lest he not fulfill his obligation with what his Creator graciously gave him, to give to the poor.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:25: And so, among the things that bring a person to submission of heart is considering what we explained in the Gate of Fear, in several aspects, that sin darkens the soul, blemishes the supernal worlds, and causes the exile of the Shechinah - and then he shall think within himself and say in his heart, it would be better for him not to have been created, since he causes so much evil.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:26: And therefore it is fitting for a person to flee from pride and dominion, for pride is the root of all bad attributes, and brings a person to several sins, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 23a), on the verse (Leviticus 4:22), "when [asher] a ruler [nasi] sins" - these are its words: Rabbi Yitzchak taught, why is it different, that everywhere else it is written "if" [im], as in (ibid. 4:3), "if the anointed priest sins," and "if the whole congregation of Israel errs" (ibid. 4:13), but here, "when a ruler sins," and it is not written "and if a ruler sins" - what is the intent? Rather, these priests are not found sinning this way, for they always guard themselves, since their Master's burden is upon them every day, and the burden of all of Israel, and the burden of every single one - and therefore it is a wonder when they sin, and therefore "if" is written. And likewise, "and if the whole congregation of Israel errs" - it is a wonder, that all of them be found in one sin, for if these sin, those would not sin - and therefore "if" is written. But "when a ruler sins" - certainly, because his heart is haughty within him, and the people go after him and are appointed under him - and therefore "when a ruler sins," such as one who transgressed a negative commandment and did one of them - and therefore "if" is not written of him, since his words were not in doubt - to this point. And so, before this in the same parashah, at the end of page 8, it says, and all sins are found only among the wealthy, since their heart is haughty within them, and are not found among the poor. And therefore it is fitting for a person to distance himself from lordship and dominion, so that his heart not become proud and sin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:27: And honor is one of the things that removes one from this world and the World to Come - from this world, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Tractate Berachot (55a): three things shorten a person's days, and one of them is conducting oneself with authority - for Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said, why did Joseph die before his brothers? Because he conducted himself with authority over them - to this point. And so this teaching is found in Sotah (13b). Rabbi Yochanan said, woe to authority, which buries its holders (Pesachim 87b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:28: And further, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, elaborated at length in the Pesikta (Rabbati, chapter 22) on the verse (Proverbs 6:32), "he who commits adultery with a woman lacks heart," how fitting it is to distance oneself - these are its words: Rabbi Menachma in the name of Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiya, Rabbi Mani in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zevida: "he who commits adultery with a woman lacks heart" - whoever accepts authority upon himself in order to benefit from it is nothing but like this adulterer, who benefits from a woman's body. "He destroys his own soul who does it" - like Moses, as it is said (Exodus 32:32), "and now, if You will forgive their sin - but if not, blot me out, please"; like Joshua, who said (Joshua 7:8), "O LORD, [what can I say] - by me [rather than] by them"; like David, who said (I Chronicles 21:17), "let Your hand, please, be against me and against my father's house, but not a plague against Your people."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:29: Rabbi Menachma bar Yaakov brings it from here (Proverbs 25:8), "do not hastily go out to quarrel" - it is written [as an instruction] to a great one [rav]: never run after authority. Why? Lest [you fail] in what you shall do in the end, when your fellow humiliates you - tomorrow they come and ask you questions, what shall you answer. Rabbi Ze'ira brings it from here, "you shall not bear/take up [lo tisa]" (Exodus 20:7) - if Scripture speaks of a false oath, it has already been said (Leviticus 19:12), "and you shall not swear falsely by My Name" - what then does "you shall not take up" teach? That you shall not accept authority upon yourself when you are not fit for authority. Rabbi Abahu said, I am called holy and you are called holy - behold, if you do not have all the attributes that I have, do not accept authority upon yourself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:30: "He who commits adultery with a woman lacks heart" - the Holy One, blessed be He, removes wisdom from his heart, and there is no "wisdom" except Torah, as it is said (Psalms 19:8), "making the simple wise" - and moreover, the radiance of his face is changed, and when he comes to the day of judgment, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not forgive him, but rather is filled with wrath against him, as it is said (Proverbs 6:34), "and he will not spare on the day of vengeance" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:31: And further, concerning his punishment in the World to Come, they said in Tractate Rosh Hashanah, first chapter (17a): but the Sadducees, the informers, and the heretics who denied the Torah, who denied the resurrection of the dead, who separated from the ways of the community, and who spread their terror in the land of the living, and so on, descend to Gehinnom and are judged there for generations of generations, as it is said (Isaiah 66:24), "and they shall go out and see the corpses of the men who transgressed against Me," and so on - Gehinnom ceases but they do not cease, as it is said (Psalms 49:15), "and their form is for Sheol to consume," and so on. And we say further there, "and who spread their terror in the land of the living" - Rav Chisda said, this is a communal leader who casts excessive fear upon the community not for the sake of Heaven. Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav, any communal leader who casts excessive fear upon the community not for the sake of Heaven does not merit to see a son who is a Torah scholar, as it is said (Job 37:24), "therefore men fear Him; He does not regard any who are wise of heart" - to this point. It follows that the punishment of one who pursues authority has punishment in this world and punishment in the World to Come without measure, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:32: And haughtiness of spirit removed Jeroboam son of Nevat from the World to Come - and so they said in Sanhedrin (101b): Rav Nachman said, the haughtiness of spirit that was in Jeroboam drove him from the World to Come, as it is said (I Kings 12:26), "and Jeroboam said in his heart, now the kingdom will return to the house of David; if this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD... and they shall return," and so on, "to Rehoboam king of Judah" - he said, it is a tradition that sitting in the [Temple] courtyard is only for the kings of the house of David alone; when they see him sitting and me standing, they will say, this one is king and that one is not king, and they shall kill me - and everyone shall go to him [Rehoboam]. Immediately (ibid. 12:28), "and the king took counsel, and made two golden calves" - he said to them, it is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:33: And moreover, even a Torah scholar, if he is proud of his wisdom, his wisdom departs and he forgets his learning, as we say in Pesachim (66b): Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav, whoever is arrogant - if he is a prophet, his prophecy departs from him, and if he is a sage, his wisdom departs. If he is a sage, from where do we know this? From Hillel - for the master said, he began to taunt them with words and said to them, what caused you that I had to come up from Babylon and become your prince? The laziness that was in you, that you did not serve the two great men of the generation, Shemaya and Avtalyon - and he said to them, this halachah I have heard and forgotten. If he is a prophet, that his prophecy departs, from where do we know this? From Devorah, as it is said (Judges 5:7), "the villages ceased," and so on, "until I, Devorah, arose," and so on, and it is written (ibid. 5:12), "awake, awake, Devorah" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:34: And so they said in the Midrash on the verse (Job 9:7), "who commands the sun and it does not rise" - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yalkut, Job, remez 904): and so you find with the greatest of the prophets - because he said (Deuteronomy 1:17), "and the matter that is too hard for you," the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, by your life, even a ruling that women know, you do not know, as it is said (Numbers 27:5), "and Moses brought their case before the LORD," and it is written (ibid. 27:7), "the daughters of Zelophehad speak rightly" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 2:35: And further we say in Kiddushin (49b), concerning what we say, ten kabin of haughtiness of spirit descended to the world - nine were taken by Elam and one by the whole rest of the world - and it raised a difficulty: but did haughtiness of spirit not descend to Babylon? And so on, and it raised a further difficulty: but the master has said, the sign of haughtiness of spirit is poverty, and poverty is [found] only in Babylon? What is "poverty"? Poverty of Torah, as it is written (Song of Songs 8:8), "we have a little sister" - Rabbi Yochanan said, this is Elam, which merited to learn but did not merit to teach - to this point.
